newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses head for records, lira dearer.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses head for records, lira dearer.

text.p: European bourses started bullishly on Monday on the back of yet another record closing high on Wall Street and the lira, buoyed by re-entry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), strengthened against the mark.

London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, was 32 points or 0.8 percent up at 4051.3 by 1000 GMT, extending a late Friday surge sparked by optimism over Tuesday's budget, a fresh outbreak of bid speculation and the latest record peak on Wall Street, which saw an almost two percent rise over the course of last week.
On the foreign exchanges, a focus was the lira, which was bought against the mark after the weekend news that it would re-join Europe's ERM grid at 990 per-mark mid-point.
Italy had been ejected from the ERM in 1992 by a wall of foreign exchange bets against the lira.

At 1000 GMT it had firmed sharply to around 991 to the mark compared with 999.15 late in Europe on Friday. "I think a lot of the good news has been priced in for the lira, so I would be surprised if there was much more large-scale buying of lira," said a trader at a Swiss Bank.
The dollar was firm against the mark and yen in early Europe but just below overnight peaks.
Analysts said it had been buoyed after French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Sunday there was some margin for the dollar's appreciation.
He reiterated, however, there was no reason to change the parity between the franc and the mark.
"Every opportunity Mr Arthuis gets to go public on the need for a firmer dollar, he absolutely takes," said Brian Martin, chief foreign exchange economist at BZW.
Martin said Arthuis dollar comments and mark weakness in Europe on the back of the lira's ERM re-entry were also helping support the U.S. currency.

Traders said the London bourse was focused on the budget, hoping for a fiscally tight package that would ease pressure on interest rates to cool the pace of growth. They saw the FTSE pushing towards its intraday record of 4,073.2 set on October 21.
On Friday the blue chip index broke through 4,000 for the first time in November to close up 64.9 points, its biggest one-day gain in 16 months.

Analysts warned, however, that a statement due Monday afternoon by Chancellor Kenneth Clarke on the government's position on European monetary union could upset the market by rekindling political uncertainties ahead of an election which must be held by next May.

In Frankfurt German shares also opened floor trading well up and looked set to penetrate the 2,800 watershed on the DAX index. At 1000 GMT the DAX was up 22.5 at 2787.98 - just ten points below its record trading peak set on November 15.
Deutsche Telekom, floated last week in the largest share sale in European history, was again the heaviest-traded stock.
On the Paris bourse, French shares also opened on a higher note following a near-one percent gain on Friday.

Analysts said the underlying tone remained positive although some viewed the market as ready for a consolidation after recent gains. Fire hit Eurotunnel, however, shed 10 percent at the start after weekend press reports that its re-opening for passenger traffic could be later than the company had hoped.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.56 yen and 1.5150 marks against 111.34 yen and 1.5039 marks late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 32.6 points at 4,051.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 16.19 at 2,271.66.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 25.5 at 2,787.98.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was off sharply at $375.0 an ounce in Europe, down from Friday's close of 377.15. Silver was at $4.84.
